metadata.name: su
metadata.description: Change user ID or become root

installation.note: su is a core system command available on all Linux systems

overview.summary: su (substitute user) starts a shell or runs a command as another user, most commonly root. Without a username, it defaults to root. Unlike sudo, su typically requires the target user's password (root's by default).
when_to_use: Become root or another user for administrative tasks
Run a command as another user (su -c)
Switch to a different user's environment for testing

syntax.description: If USER is omitted, root is assumed. Use - or -l for a login shell (loads target user's profile).

options.description: Start a login shell (load USER's environment, cd to home)
options.use_case: Fully become root or another user (recommended for root)

options.description: Run a single command as the target user
options.use_case: Run one command as root or another user

options.description: Use the specified shell instead of default

examples.title: Become root (login shell)
examples.description: Switch to root with root's environment (prompts for root password)

examples.title: Run one command as root
examples.description: Execute a single command as root
examples.use_case: One-off root command without staying root

common_pitfalls.description: su asks for the target user's password (often root); sudo asks for your password and uses /etc/sudoers.
common_pitfalls.solution: Prefer sudo for routine admin if configured; use su - when you need a full root login shell.

related_commands.description: Run commands as root (or other user) using your password and sudoers
